clue.text: Fawlty in charge of a church

parts.note: Basil Fawlty is the hotelier played by John Cleese in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: The notorious hotelier has somehow been put in charge of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is an oblong church building, especially one granted special status by the Pope.

clue.text: Opening action at cricket?

parts.note: before a cricket match begins the captains flip a coin to decide who bats first, so this is literally the opening action

explanation.surface: A question about how a cricket innings gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests the first ball or the opening batsmen, but the very first action of a match is the captains' coin flip.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin flip deciding who bats first is the first thing that happens in any cricket match.

clue.text: Was chief of detectives: rank?

parts.note: to run an organisation is to be in charge of it, so was chief of gives ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police forces

explanation.surface: A question asking whether heading the detective squad confers rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a noun for police status, but here it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means stinking or gone off, just like butter that has turned sour.

clue.text: Stupidly deter run to be elected as MP

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A candidate foolishly discourages running, yet still wins a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics a candidate is said to be returned to Parliament when voters choose them as their member.

clue.text: Cash standard in unstable Pacific region

definitions.meaning: a classic song recorded by the country singer Johnny Cash
the horseshoe of volcanoes and earthquake zones around the Pacific Ocean

explanation.surface: Talk of a monetary standard operating within a shaky part of the Pacific economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash standard' reads like a gold standard for money, but Cash is Johnny Cash and the standard is one of his best-known songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a famous Johnny Cash song title and the name of the volcanic belt circling the Pacific basin.

clue.text: Cooks' company on board

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it, so the company sits within the ship letters

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and SS is the usual abbreviation for steamship
a company of people working together is a team

explanation.surface: A phrase about the ship's cooks being a crew of their own aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the apostrophe in 'Cooks'' as 'Cooks is'; the verb sense of cooking, not the chefs, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming food over boiling water is one way of cooking it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Soldiers wearing hat that gives a wide view

indicators.note: a hat wearer has it around their head, so here the hat surrounds the soldiers

parts.note: a Panama is a lightweight straw hat
OR stands for Other Ranks, the ordinary soldiers of the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers sport a brimmed hat that lets them see across the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is an unbroken sweeping view of a whole region in every direction.

clue.text: An inspiring problem

parts.note: inspiring here means breathing in, so this is a problem with drawing breath rather than a motivating puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' usually means motivating, but its literal sense is inhaling; the problem is a breathing disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: This chronic condition narrows the airways, making inhalation difficult — literally a difficulty with taking breath in.

clue.text: Is pushing spades through leaves

indicators.note: pushing the card suit through something forces it into the middle, so one piece goes inside the other
through says the letter for spades passes into the midst of the word for departures

parts.note: leaves as a verb means departs or exits
S is the abbreviation for the card suit spades

explanation.surface: A gardener describes forcing a spade through fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests foliage beside 'spades', but it is the verb for departing.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, so the third-person form is a straight synonym for 'is'.

clue.text: Teases children

definitions.meaning: verb: jokes with or ribs someone playfully

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both makes fun of someone in jest and young offspring, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Persian thief?

parts.note: a Persian is a breed of cat, so a Persian thief would be a feline burglar — the term for a nimble burglar who climbs in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian' suggests someone from Iran, but it is the long-haired cat breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an agile housebreaker who climbs walls, and read literally it is a feline robber, which a Persian might be.

clue.text: Shrank back as gale enveloped church

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap around, so the gale surrounds the church

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone recoils as a storm swirls around the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or recoil in pain or embarrassment is to shrink back.

clue.text: Simple supper: about time a piece got cooked

indicators.note: about can mean in disorder or all over the place, so it sets up a rearrangement
cooked as in cooked the books means falsified or altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A homely meal: it is about time a portion got cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means C (circa) wrapping something, but there is no C to spare: with 'cooked' it signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat topped with mashed potato is a classic plain, homely British evening dish.

clue.text: Isn't fame ridiculously obvious?

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests something absurdly out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: surely celebrity is absurdly plain to see?
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is plainly evident to the eye or mind, needing no proof.

clue.text: Real force applied to concrete

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
concrete as an adjective means real or actual rather than abstract

explanation.surface: A builder speaks of real force being applied to wet concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concrete' reads as the building material, but it is the adjective meaning tangible.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual describes what is true and based on fact, so it serves as a synonym for real.

clue.text: Patronage of USA epics doubtful

indicators.note: doubtful implies uncertain or unsettled, so these letters are not in their final order

explanation.surface: A sponsor backing American blockbusters is a dubious arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their support, protection or sponsorship.

clue.text: Counsellor these days in need of sunshade

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the current era, hence these days
a visor is a peak or shield that keeps sun out of the eyes

explanation.surface: A therapist nowadays needs something to keep the sun off.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser, also spelt this way, gives guidance professionally, as a counsellor does.

clue.text: Ancient distinction in national flag

parts.note: ancient means old
distinction in the sense of honour or renown is glory

explanation.surface: A historic honour embodied in a country's banner.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the popular nickname of the Stars and Stripes, the flag of the United States.

clue.text: Create one new hole

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a vent is an opening or hole letting air or gas out

explanation.surface: Instructions to make a fresh opening in something.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise or originate something that did not exist before is to create it.

clue.text: Killer finds a pair of idiots at home

indicators.note: a pair means two, so the word for an idiot appears twice over

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: A murderer discovers two fools sitting in their house.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, specifically one who kills a prominent person for political reasons or pay.

clue.text: European country imprisons king? That's a wrench

indicators.note: to imprison is to hold within walls, so the country surrounds the king

parts.note: Spain is a country of Europe
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A news item: a European state jails its monarch, a painful wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrench' looks like an emotional upheaval, but it is the twisting injury to a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench in the sense of a sharp twist of a joint is an ankle or wrist injury of exactly this kind.

clue.text: You and I wearing Edward's country outfit?

indicators.note: the clothes one wears go around the body, so the Edward piece wraps the pronoun

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward, and with the possessive gives Ted's
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: We are dressed in Edward's country clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Woollen cloth suits and jackets are the traditional dress of the British country gentleman, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Military display is tawdry stuff, as well

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods
as well means too or also

explanation.surface: A sniffy verdict that a parade of soldiers is also cheap rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' might suggest a skin design, but the sense is a show of marching bands such as the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an evening show of drill and music performed by armed forces, as at Edinburgh.

clue.text: Outstanding temper — nine injured

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A furious outburst leaves nine people hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' reads as a rage but is just letters for the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surpassing all others in their field stands out above them, which is what outstanding means.

clue.text: Man's meal spoiled

definitions.note: possessive used as an adjective meaning of or belonging to a man

indicators.note: food that is spoiled is ruined and messed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man's dinner has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' is the definition, read as an adjective: of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Male describes what pertains to men, so it can stand for the possessive 'man's'.

clue.text: Keep it off clothes: some harm, otherwise

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice to keep something away from garments, as it would do some harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes larvae chew wool, so wardrobes are guarded with cedar or mothballs to keep this insect away.

clue.text: Piece of fish, I note, not unlimited

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's note on a strictly limited supply of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Finite means having bounds or limits, the opposite of infinite.

clue.text: Horses moving along, though not on these

definitions.text: Horses moving along, though not on these

parts.words: Horses moving along, though not on these
parts.note: the word names horses bred to race at a trot, and also pigs' feet, which horses do not move on

explanation.walkthrough: The same word means trotting horses and pigs' feet cooked as food, so horses trot but never on these.
explanation.definitionFit: Both racing horses trained to trot and the feet of pigs share this one name.
